 - Meteorological Overview:

Upper level ridging over the Western CONUS early this morning will 
continue to be flattened as a potent shortwave over the Gulf of 
Alaska slides east over British Columbia and the Canadian Prairie 
Provinces through the day today. Increasing cross barrier flow over 
the Northern Rockies will lead to strengthening southwest to west 
winds across Southwest through North Central Montana, most notably 
along the Rocky Mountain Front and International Border. These 
downsloping southwest to west winds will lead to another day of 
above normal temperatures across the region, with highs peaking in 
the mid-60s to near 70 degrees in the valleys of Southwest and 
Central Montana to the low 70s to near 80 degrees over the plains of 
Central and North Central Montana.  "Cooler" temperatures are then 
expected into the day on Sunday in wake of a weak Pacific front, 
which will slide east and over the Northern Rockies late tonight, 
with highs topping out in the upper 50s to low 60s. Despite 
persistent zonal flow over the Northern Rockies on Sunday weak 
surface high pressure settling in over the Pacific Northwest and 
Northern Rockies will help to support light surfaces winds and 
continued dry conditions. - Moldan 

By Monday morning, weak ridging takes its place as an upper level 
trough begins to move down the Pacific Coast towards northern 
California. This will create southwesterly flow aloft by Monday 
evening, which will last through the middle of next week, allowing 
for seasonably average temperatures. By Thursday, the trough will 
have moved south of the Great Basin, creating a more direct 
southerly flow aloft, before moving northeast towards Wyoming. This 
will allow temperatures to warm on Thursday before cooling down on 
Friday. Increased moisture aloft will get carried north by the upper 
level southerly low, increasing precipitation chances towards the 
end of next week into next weekend. There remains shearing and 
splitting in the trough late Thursday into next weekend, so while 
one can expect cooling temperatures and increased precipitation 
chances late in the forecast period, confidence in the forecast 
specifics for this time remains low. -Dzomba


 - Forecast Confidence & Scenarios:

High Winds through this evening...

Confidence is very high that High Winds will develop along and west 
of a Sweet Grass, to Cut Bank, to Dupuyer, to Choteau, to Augusta 
line by the late morning hours today and persist through the evening 
hours tonight. The strongest winds within the region are likely to 
occur across the Blackfeet Nation, most notably in and near the 
Browning and Heart Butte communities where isolated wind gusts 
approaching 90 mph will be possible. Where confidence begins to 
decrease is for areas east of Cut Bank along the US Hwy 2 corridor, 
with the exception of areas immediately downwind of the Sweet Grass 
Hills where localized strong winds will occur due to mountain wave 
activity. Confidence is lower for these areas along the US Hwy 2 
corridor given limited support for deep mixing within BUFKIT data; 
however, with 60kts at H700 overspreading these areas within a 
favorable window for mixing and subsequent momentum transfer to the 
surface it will not take much for strong winds to materialize across 
Hill and Blaine counties. For now I will hold course with not 
expanding the areal footprint of the High Wind Warning further east, 
but there is a 10% chance that wind gusts could exceed 60 mph in 
Hill and Northern Blaine counties; in addition to the wind prone 
areas along the northern slopes of the Little Belt Mountains.
